title: Lead: your own manual, silent sessions, and handing a skill back by evidence
outcomes: Tells an exercise that shows unprompted skill from one that names the idea
Runs a silent session and records first-try results and which habits he used unprompted
Decides from a small ledger which skill to hand back to coached mode and which has too little data
Writes a one-page manual for a month: routine, evidence, hand-back rule, one thing done with another person

steps.text: To **lead** is to run the routine yourself while the app only keeps the record. Help should fade on **evidence** that you do something unprompted, session after session. A rating summarises game results; it does not show which habits you use without being asked. A **silent session** turns hints off so that what you do alone shows. Solving an exercise that names the idea shows less than solving one that does not.

steps.title: Same position, the idea named or not
steps.prompt: The board you just saw is the unprompted version of the position you solved, shown with its answer marked. Predict about the named version.

steps.text: **What the record can and cannot see.** The Progress page counts your first attempts at unlabeled exercises (nothing names the idea or the theme): hints used and right without hints, by week, with all skills pooled. Its skill table gives running totals, not weeks. It does not show your habits, your thinking time, or games played elsewhere. So your manual needs a second record, your own: after a silent session, note which habits you used unprompted, and tally results per skill.

steps.prompt: Session note: four silent positions, no hints.

fields.label: How many of the four did you get right on the first try?
Did you run your own routine (for example: list checks, captures and threats) without anything telling you to?
One thing I did that no prompt asked for, or one thing I skipped:

steps.text: **Hand back on evidence.** Handing a skill back to **coached mode** (hints on, lessons and named exercises again) should follow your record, not a mood. The Progress table shows, week by week, how often you used hints and how often you were right without them. **Rule of thumb** (a first guess): judge a skill only after 8 or more hint-free attempts in all, and send it back if accuracy without hints stays under half in both weeks. A small fictional ledger follows.

steps.prompt: Press Save note to see the answers. Fictional ledger, two weeks, first attempts at exercises that do not name the idea. Hints is the share of attempts where you opened a hint; right counts only attempts without a hint. Forks: hints 50% then 10%; right 4 of 6, then 8 of 9. Pins: hints 20% then 20%; right 3 of 8, then 3 of 8. Skewers: right 2 of 2, then 1 of 2. Rule of thumb (a first guess): judge a skill after 8 or more hint-free attempts in all; send it back to coached mode if accuracy without hints stays under half in both weeks.

fields.label: Which skill has too little data to judge?
By the rule, which skill goes back to coached mode?
Forks: hints fell from 50% to 10% while accuracy rose. What does the rule say?
One way this rule could mislead me:

steps.text: **What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** Silent practice is a checkbox on the Practice page: hints off, answers shown afterwards. Today lets you set your own aim first, and Progress keeps the weekly record. The thinking prompts for loop levels 1-3 retire after five mixed solves in a row with them closed (five is a first guess). Nothing hands a skill back for you. Saved notes export from Settings, but there is no manual page: keep your manual in your own file.

steps.prompt: Write your manual for one month, with no system prompts: the app only keeps the record. Working alone is not automatically good practice; one study of chess players (reported second-hand, not re-checked here) found practice with others mattered in its sample. So include one thing you do with someone else.
